endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Conditional deployment with enhanced monitoring — Deploy in a limited, constrained context with explicit safeguards, heightened monitoring, and a defined re-evaluation date. Conditions must be documented and enforced.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: ID.AM-4: External information systems are catalogued

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Connect new GAI policies, procedures, and processes to existing model, data, software development, and IT governance and to legal, compliance, and risk management activities.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether inventorying AI infrastructure and connected external systems prevents cascading failures, and no study documents how often such failures occur. The recommendation currently rests on three governance frameworks that describe or encourage cataloguing and linking AI to existing IT governance.

perspectives.view: Zero studies test the practice and zero studies document the hazard, so certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The endorsements are expert frameworks rather than empirical findings. One endorsement, the CHAI playbook statement on conditional deployment, addresses documented safeguards generally and bears only indirectly on infrastructure inventory.

The CHAI Assurance Standards Guide lists cataloguing of external information systems (ID.AM-4), and NIST AI 600-1 says new generative AI processes should connect to existing IT governance and risk management. These are voluntary frameworks. Their language suggests that auditors and accreditors may come to expect an inventory, but none of the supplied sources makes it a legal requirement.

The hazard, cascading failures when infrastructure or connected systems change, is plausible, but no supplied study measures its frequency or harm severity. Without that data, a health system cannot estimate how many errors an inventory would catch before they reach patients.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that document how often changes to computing infrastructure or connected systems cause AI failures in clinical settings, and that compare failure detection and recovery time between organizations with and without maintained inventories of AI infrastructure and external connections.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence exists for Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net systems with older or fragmented IT may face different connection risks and fewer staff to maintain an inventory, and the supplied sources do not address that difference.
